# Rollback Drill Decision: Atlas Rehearsals

**Date:** 2026-07-02
**Participants:** Quinton Fairweather (CTO)

Quinton: "Atlas rollback rehearsals run monthly from now on. A rollback
we have not rehearsed is a rollback we do not actually have."

Key decisions:
- **Cadence**: monthly Atlas rollback rehearsals
- **Owner**: Quinton Fairweather

segments.exact: Atlas rollback rehearsals run monthly from now on.
segments.note: Declarative: the utterance institutes a new recurring practice, not merely describes one.

segments.exact:
A rollback
we have not rehearsed is a rollback we do not actually have.
segments.note: Justifying assertion for the preceding declarative.
Bullet restating the cadence decision; unified with Quinton's voice as the decision's owner/source.
Ownership assignment recorded as part of the same decisions summary.

observations.why: Establishes a forward-looking cadence for a specific named rehearsal practice.

evidence.quote: is a rollback we do not actually have

observations.why: Counterfactual conditional: a hypothetical untested rollback framed as a general principle about what one possesses.
Labels a planned, recurring cadence for a specific named activity.
Names a specific person as the current owner of the rehearsal practice.

evidence.quote:
A rollback
we have not rehearsed is a rollback we do not actually have.

observations.why: Aphoristic urgency framing — an unrehearsed rollback equated to having none at all — carries high-arousal negative valence: alarm that the unpracticed plan is no plan.

evidence.quote:
A rollback
we have not rehearsed is a rollback we do not actually have.

observations.why: Aphoristic maxim that crystallizes a rule into matched opposition — the document's register signature, plain-spoken but maxim-shaped.

mints.name: RuleAsMatchedOpposition
mints.title: a rollback we have not rehearsed is a rollback we do not actually have
mints.frame: Is the rule here crystallized into a matched opposition of clauses, so that the phrasing itself carries the mandate?

evidence.quote:
A rollback
we have not rehearsed is a rollback we do not actually have.

observations.why: Parallel syntactic frame ('A rollback we … is a rollback we …') sets rehearsed against unrehearsed in deliberate contrast — the unrehearsed rollback is negated as something you 'do not actually have.'

mints.name: UnrehearsedIsUnowned
mints.title: a rollback we have not rehearsed is a rollback we do not actually have
mints.frame: Is the claim being crystallized into a matched opposition that equates not-rehearsed with not-possessed?

observations.why: Establishing a recurring rehearsal cadence appeals to security/stability (conservation) and to maintaining capability (competence).
Framing an unrehearsed rollback as one you lack asserts that genuine capability requires practiced mastery — a competence appeal grounded in security.
Restating the cadence as a structured specification reinforces the security/stability value of a maintained routine.
Naming an owner appeals to self-origination — the rehearsal program is someone's own responsibility to direct.

mints.name: UnrehearsedCapabilityIsNotCapability
mints.title: a rollback we have not rehearsed is a rollback we do not actually have
mints.frame: Is the text asserting that a capability only exists when it has been practiced — that unexercised readiness is no readiness at all?

observations.why: Speaker asserts a cadence as decided policy, invoking positional authority to set the schedule.

evidence.quote:
A rollback
we have not rehearsed is a rollback we do not actually have.

observations.why: Aphoristic equivalence frames an unrehearsed rollback as no rollback at all, arguing from logic and controlling the definitional fact.
Boldface cadence label asserts the schedule as settled, reinforcing positional authority over the decision.
Self-assignment of the owner role claims authority over the rehearsal process by naming the position-holder.

mints.name: EquivalenceAsDefinition
mints.title: a thing we have not rehearsed is a thing we do not actually have
mints.frame: Is the speaker asserting control by equating an unpracticed capability with its absence, collapsing the distinction into a definitional identity?

observations.why: Operational directive with forward-permanence phrasing ('from now on') performs a settled, load-bearing decision the speaker expects others to act on.

evidence.quote:
A rollback
we have not rehearsed is a rollback we do not actually have.

observations.why: Identity-level bedrock stated as constitutive creed — an unrehearsed rollback is defined out of existence; the aphoristic form signals permanence, not a moveable claim.
Structured cadence entry ratifies the monthly rehearsal as a settled operational commitment; the formatting itself performs the settling.
Assigning a named owner ratifies accountability for the decision; the performed declarative settles who acts on it.

mints.name: UnrehearsedCapabilityDefinedOutOfExistence
mints.title: a capability we have not rehearsed is a capability we do not actually have
mints.frame: Is the conviction here asserting that an unexercised capability is definitionally absent, treating rehearsal as constitutive of possession?

positions.why: Both expressions state the same fact — monthly Atlas rollback rehearsals — but in two different registers: src-1 as a plain declarative decree ('run monthly from now on'), src-3 as a structured spec-sheet entry ('Cadence: monthly Atlas rollback rehearsals'). The directional reads align: both enact authority-ranking (a cadence set unilaterally, not proposed) and both sit in the 'decision' conviction region rather than the 'principle' region src-2 occupies. Grouping them reads the cadence as one settled fact restated in two forms, not two separate commitments.

placements.why: The envelope sets a recurring operational cadence (monthly Atlas rollback rehearsals) and names a single accountable owner (Quinton Fairweather) — this is organizational governance content, not architecture or product content, and no strata category exists yet in this repo to hold it. It is the kind of category future envelopes about cadences, ownership, and operational rituals will keep feeding, so it earns a standalone strata mint rather than folding into a leaf.

placements.why: src-2 states the constitutive principle as an aphorism — an unrehearsed rollback is definitionally not possessed — and src-1/src-3 (the monthly cadence decree, restated twice) plus src-4 (the named owner) are the concrete operational instantiation of that principle: the rehearsal cadence and ownership exist precisely to convert an assumed rollback capability into a proven one. This passes the narrative grain test — it names a subject (rehearsal-as-proof-of-capability) that future envelopes about drills, DR readiness, or other practiced-vs-assumed capabilities will keep feeding, rather than stating a one-time fact.
